clue.text: Skip the sauce

definitions.meaning: to skip is to leap about playfully, to frisk
the pickled flower bud that flavours a classic sauce served with mutton

explanation.definitionFit: A frisky leap is a caper, and capers are the pickled buds behind the well-known caper sauce.

clue.text: One who hawks tar at a low price?

parts.note: cheap means costing little
a tar and a jack are both old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sailor selling his goods cut-price is a pedlar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapjack was a pedlar selling cheap wares at fairs and markets.

clue.text: Advertisements for pants?

definitions.meaning: exaggerated promotional notices or plugs
to pant is to breathe hard and short, as when out of breath

explanation.definitionFit: A plug is a puff, and a person short of breath gasps or puffs.

clue.text: The reverse of dominant when the House is not sitting ?

definitions.meaning: in genetics a trait masked by a dominant one

definitions.text: when the House is not sitting
definitions.meaning: Parliament's break from business is a recess

explanation.definitionFit: Genes that are masked are the opposite of dominant ones; the word also hints at Parliament's recess when the House is adjourned.

clue.text: For pernicious disease I fast

parts.note: a pest is an old word for a plague or pestilence
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone vows to fast to ward off a deadly disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something deadly or harmful, spreading ruin like a plague.

clue.text: Blind detective is one in the ranks

definitions.meaning: a ... eye with no eye, so the remaining word
the lowest rank of soldier in the army

explanation.definitionFit: Take the 'eye' from the slang name for a hired investigator and the word left is the army's lowest rank.

clue.text: Metalworker or fisherman?

definitions.meaning: one who extracts metal from ore by heating it
the smelt is a small fish, so one who catches smelts

explanation.definitionFit: A worker who melts ore for its metal has this name, and jokingly so does an angler after smelt.

clue.text: I married physical education student with drive

parts.note: PE is the school abbreviation for physical education
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A married PE student shows plenty of motivation.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to propel or drive forward.

clue.text: Rent us one new building in confidence

indicators.note: the letters are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone whispers that a new building has rented them a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means between ourselves, said of something told privately.

clue.text: Irritable examination by yesterday's leader

parts.note: a test is an examination

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone is cross after the exam set by yesterday's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy means tetchy, easily annoyed.

clue.text: Successful impression I have made

parts.note: an effect is the impression something makes on the mind
've is the contracted form of have

explanation.surface: An artist proud that the impression they made worked well.
explanation.definitionFit: Something successful produces the intended result, which is to say it works.

clue.text: Ways in which love might enter to arouse pity

indicators.note: the answer is the word that love would get into to make the word for pity, so love is taken back out of that word

parts.note: pathos is the quality that arouses pity
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Musing on the routes by which love could find its way to stir compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is told backwards: put O (love) into the answer and you get PATHOS (pity), so the answer is PATHOS with its O removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths are routes or tracks, just as ways are.

clue.text: Stops odd jobs

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gives up doing little household tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd jobs' reads as one phrase, but 'odd' is the anagram signal working on 'Stops'.
explanation.definitionFit: Posts are positions of employment, in other words jobs.

clue.text: Blood-vessel has internal injury in fighting arm

indicators.note: the blood-vessel word holds the next piece inside itself

parts.note: an artery is a blood vessel carrying blood from the heart
ill as a noun means harm or injury

explanation.surface: A medical report of a soldier's arm with an internal wound to a blood vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting arm' sounds like a wounded limb, but it means a branch of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The artillery is the branch of an army that operates big guns, one of its combat arms.

clue.text: A song that is ruined is torture

indicators.note: a ruined thing is wrecked and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A music critic says a botched song is agony to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to suffer or inflict torment, as torture does.

clue.text: Bow to orderly officer in case of trouble

parts.note: an OBE is an Officer of the Order of the British Empire, an officer of an order

indicators.note: trouble disturbs things, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier bows to the duty officer in case of difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly officer' is a real army duty, but here it is an officer of an Order, OBE; 'of trouble' makes ISANCE from 'in case'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a respectful gesture such as a bow or curtsy.

clue.text: Russian forest tree ?

parts.note: red was the colour of Soviet Russia, so a Russian Communist is a Red
a wood is a small forest

explanation.surface: Asking which tree grows in a Russian forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant Californian sequoia is a tree with reddish timber.

clue.text: Distraction, so amusing

definitions.meaning: turning attention aside
entertaining, providing fun

explanation.definitionFit: Turning someone's attention away is a distraction, and an entertaining show is called this too.

clue.text: Nullified document about South Helensburgh

indicators.note: the document word goes around the remaining pieces

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
Troy was the city of Helen, a burgh being a town

explanation.surface: A deed about a Scottish town is declared void.
explanation.walkthrough: Helensburgh is a real town on the Clyde, but here it is Helen's burgh, Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nullified is cancelled entirely, wrecked beyond use.

clue.text: Rings for attendants

definitions.meaning: guard rings worn to stop a more precious ring slipping off a finger
people who look after something, such as zoo or museum staff

explanation.definitionFit: A guard ring holding another ring in place is so named, and so are people in charge of animals or buildings.

clue.text: A new day for National Union of Students

definitions.text: A new day for National Union of Students

parts.words: A new day for National Union of Students
parts.note: dawn, with the initials NUS turned around to read as the star of daytime followed by a word for going up

explanation.surface: A fresh start for the student union.
explanation.walkthrough: NUS reversed is SUN, and in a down entry the letters go up, so they 'rise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak, when the day star appears, marks a new day.

clue.text: Recommends Sid to save the. change

indicators.note: change here means alter the order of the letters of the two words before

explanation.surface: Someone recommends that Sid put money by against a change.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone on what to do is to recommend a course to them.

clue.text: What difficult art, making a crossword

indicators.note: a difficult arrangement suggests the letters of the two words are worked over

explanation.surface: Setters discussing how hard the art of compiling puzzles is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossword' is not a puzzle but a cross word: a word meaning across.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart means across or crosswise, so it is literally a word for crossing.

clue.text: December-not only in January

parts.note: the name for December is true only when the present is the first month of the year, as the period just gone

explanation.surface: A riddle about the one month when December takes another name.
explanation.walkthrough: Seen from January, December is the period just past.
explanation.definitionFit: Only in January does December earn the description of the period immediately before the present one.

clue.text: Did she languish in Asia Minor?

definitions.meaning: the heroine of Sheridan's play The Rivals, surnamed Languish
an ancient kingdom in what is now western Turkey

explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's romantic heroine Miss Languish has this first name, and it is also an ancient realm in Anatolia.

clue.text: Contemplated Frenchman's character at second hand

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, the French form of address
used goods are second-hand

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's personality, formed second-hand, was pondered.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or reflect deeply.

clue.text: Turner gives lift to airborne type

definitions.meaning: something that turns or spins
the spinning blades that lift a helicopter into the air

explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part of a machine is so called, and the spinning blade assembly that raises a helicopter has the same name.

clue.text: Area where car overturned in a race

indicators.note: the reversed car goes inside the race letters

parts.note: the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race

indicators.note: an overturned car is upside down, so in a down clue its letters run the other way

explanation.surface: Locating the spot where a vehicle flipped during a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is an expanse of land, a stretch or area.

clue.text: Oranges and lemons saint's European followers

definitions.text: Oranges and lemons saint's European followers

parts.words: Oranges and lemons saint's European followers
parts.note: the nursery rhyme's bells of St Clement's, and the word that follows that saint's name in a London church, which is also a Scandinavian nationality

explanation.surface: Fruit-loving followers of a saint, as if a church congregation from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Oranges and Lemons' opens with 'say the bells of St Clement's'; the London church St Clement Danes puts a Scandinavian people after the saint.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Denmark are Europeans, and their name follows St Clement in the church's title.

clue.text: Like the conversations of a savage writer

definitions.text: Like the conversations of a savage writer

parts.words: Like the conversations of a savage writer
parts.note: Walter Savage Landor wrote a famous series of invented dialogues between historical figures; savage is his middle name, not a description

explanation.surface: Wondering what a fierce author's talk would be like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'savage' is the middle name of the poet Walter Savage Landor, whose best-known work is a set of made-up conversations.
explanation.definitionFit: Landor's dialogues were invented, existing only in fancy, which is the title word of his book.

clue.text: A change at noon intended, I hear

indicators.note: the setter says the following letters come from words heard spoken rather than seen

parts.note: at noon the a.m. period ends, giving AM END, and intended means meant

explanation.surface: Someone announces they meant to make an alteration at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Noon is where a.m. ends, so 'at noon intended' is spoken as AM END MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is an alteration, especially to a law or document.

clue.text: Penalized at Oxford, having got a wicket?

definitions.meaning: Oxford and Cambridge students were punished by being confined to college after hours
a wicket is a small gate, so this means fitted with a gate

explanation.definitionFit: A student confined to college was said to be gated, and anything with a gate fitted can be described the same way.
